gen_risks.description: Network underutilisation due to delayed or failed build-out projects
gen_risks.mitigation: Close monitoring of build-out project progress and identification of alternative users to fill spare network capacity
gen_risks.evidence: Section 2.3.1: 'build-out’ projects, Padeswood and Viridor, and top-up projects, are not within the scope of this FBC'

gen_risks.description: Cost escalation due to changes in underlying costs, supply chain cost increases, and unwinding of optimism bias
gen_risks.mitigation: Regular cost reviews and updates, and implementation of cost assurance processes
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.2.1: 'While there has been significant cost escalation since the OBC, this has largely been driven by changes in underlying costs'

gen_risks.description: Failure to achieve expected benefits due to lack of alternative abatement options for capture projects
gen_risks.mitigation: Identification of alternative abatement options and development of contingency plans
gen_risks.evidence: Section 3.3.2: 'For each capture project, we have sought to identify the most plausible alternative abatement options'

gen_risks.description: Regulatory risks due to uncertainty around subsidy control principles and compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022
gen_risks.mitigation: Close engagement with the Subsidy Advice Unit and compliance with subsidy control principles
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.2.5: 'The Track-1 CCUS Cluster Sequencing Process has been developed to align with the UK subsidy control regime'

gen_risks.description: Cross-chain risks due to interdependencies between T&SCo and capture projects
gen_risks.mitigation: Identification and allocation of cross-chain risks to the party most suited to manage them
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.1.3: 'The business models have been designed to address the key market barriers which would otherwise restrict the deployment of CCUS'

gen_risks.description: Technical risks due to complexity of CCUS technology and lack of commercial-scale deployment experience
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of technical assurance processes and identification of technical risks
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4.1.4.1: 'Technical assurance has been used in a targeted manner to test the data, assumptions, costs and risks put forward by delivery partners'

gen_risks.description: Financial risks due to uncertainty around funding requirements and budget implications
gen_risks.mitigation: Regular budget reviews and updates, and identification of financial risks
gen_risks.evidence: Section 5.1: 'The purpose of this section is to: a) assess affordability by comparing the subsidy levels in these contracts to the affordability constraints agreed with HMT'

gen_risks.description: Stakeholder risks due to lack of public awareness and understanding of CCUS technology
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of stakeholder engagement and communication strategies
gen_risks.evidence: Section 6.2: 'The CCUS programme undertook a mapping exercise of all key stakeholders as part of the OBC submission'

gen_risks.description: Environmental risks due to potential CO2 leakage and environmental impacts
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of environmental monitoring and mitigation measures

gen_risks.description: Governance risks due to complexity of post-FID operating model and need for effective coordination
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of effective governance structures and coordination mechanisms
gen_risks.evidence: Section 6.3: 'The programme needs to refresh its post-FID governance to align with the changes in roles and responsibilities'

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that government (HMG) is exposed to increased costs for Track-1 post-Financial Investment Decision (FID), and that cost pressures are unaffordable within delegated budgets. [Strategic Case risk T1SR1, Section 2.5 'Identify high level potential risks', p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Contractual mechanisms ensure HMG only takes on specific risks where appropriate, with liability limited and counterparties incentivised to control costs; governance mechanisms monitor costs and provide early warning of overruns; contingent liability exposure is accurately monitored.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the programme does not realise its intended benefits for Track-1. [Strategic Case risk T1SR3, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Projects undergo detailed technical assurance and financial due diligence; projects must meet Initial Conditions Precedent (ICPs) before contracts take effect and Operational CPs thereafter, with LCCC able to terminate and avoid paying for an underperforming project; contractual mechanisms allocate performance-related risk to the private sector; continued engagement with the global Carbon Management Challenge to expand CCUS use and deliver UK trade benefits.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the post-FID operating model across public and private sector parties will not operate successfully. [Strategic Case risk T1SR4, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: Medium/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Progress of arm's-length bodies' (ALBs') capacity (funding, resource) and capability (knowledge, skills) to operate successfully post-FID is monitored through the Delivery Board; a DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function will be set up between FID and Commercial Operations Date (COD) to mitigate risks to cluster delivery and system integration; readiness-testing mechanisms are in place ahead of FID; FY24/25 funding for the ALBs to fulfil their roles has been secured.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk of an unclear exit path for HMG from its role in the Track-1 commercial framework. [Strategic Case risk T1SR5, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Key planned developments include amendments to the process for granting economic licences, a move toward a competitive allocation process for capture contracts, and evolution of transport & storage business models to reflect an increased private-sector role in managing cross-chain risks; cost-reduction levers (UK ETS pricing, CBAMs) are intended to help cultivate a self-sustaining industry and enable an HMG exit path.
